title: TARP capital injection on bank risk-taking

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Difference-in-Differences (two-way fixed effects) with an event-study robustness check.

Why:  
• Treatment (TARP receipt) varies across banks but is constant within a bank once it enters; we observe treated and untreated banks before and after the program.  
• We exploit the timing difference (pre vs. post 2008Q4) to compare the change in the non-performing-loan (NPL) ratio of treated banks with the change in untreated banks.  

Key assumptions:  
1. Parallel-trends: In the absence of TARP, treated and control banks would have evolved similarly. We test this through an event-study pre-trend check.  
2. No differential shocks coinciding with treatment that hit treated banks only.  
3. Stable unit treatment value (no spillovers).  

## 2. R Code
```r
###############################################################
# Difference-in-Differences: TARP and bank risk-taking
# File: experiments/exp_b/data/s04_data.csv
###############################################################

### 0. Packages ------------------------------------------------
need <- c("data.table", "fixest", "ggplot2")
new  <- need[! (need %in% installed.packages()[,1])]
if(length(new)) install.packages(new, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
lapply(need, library, character.only = TRUE)

### 1. Load data ----------------------------------------------
dt <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s04_data.csv")

# Basic checks
print(head(dt))
print(summary(dt))

### 2. Difference-in-Differences ------------------------------
# Two-way FE, cluster by bank
did <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~unit_id)
print("=== DID estimate ===")
print(etable(did, se = "cluster"))

### 3. Event-study (Sun & Abraham) ----------------------------
# Construct relative time for treated banks
# Assume first post period for each treated bank is its switch date; untreated assigned Inf
dt[, first_treat_period := ifelse(treated == 1, min(period[post == 1]), Inf), by = unit_id]
dt[, rel_time := period - first_treat_period]

# Run Sun & Abraham estimator (need both cohort & calendar FE)
es <- feols(y ~ sunab(first_treat_period, period) | unit_id + period, data = dt, cluster = ~unit_id)

print("=== Event-study summary ===")
print(summary(es, agg = "-5:-1"))   # pre-trend joint F-test

# Plot event-study coefficients
iplot(es, ref.line = 0, xlab = "Quarters relative to first TARP receipt",
      main = "Event-study: Non-performing loan ratio")

### 4. Robustness checks --------------------------------------
# 4a. Add bank-specific linear time trend
dt[, t := period]
did_trend <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post + i(t, unit_id) | unit_id + period,
                   data = dt, cluster = ~unit_id)

# 4b. Exclude 2008Q4 transition quarter (period == 5, say)
did_excl <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                  data = dt[period != 5], cluster = ~unit_id)

print("=== Robustness checks ===")
etable(did, did_trend, did_excl,
       se = "cluster",
       tex = FALSE,
       headers = c("Baseline DID","+ Bank trend","Omit 2008Q4"))

### 5. Clean numeric output for replication -------------------
cat("\nPoint estimate (baseline DID) for treat_x_post:",
    coef(did)["treat_x_post"], "\n")
cat("Cluster-robust SE:",
    se(did, "cluster")["treat_x_post"], "\n")
###############################################################
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive. TARP capital injections likely relaxed regulatory and funding constraints, encouraging recipients to originate or retain riskier loans. Hence the treated × post coefficient on the NPL ratio should be > 0.

Magnitude: For large U.S. bank BHCs, prior studies find a 10–25 bp rise in NPLs; with the variable expressed in percentage points, we expect an increase of roughly 0.10–0.20 (i.e., 0.1–0.2 ppt) relative to non-recipients.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=TARP recipients, control=non-recipients; parallel pre-trends required
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: TARP banks show higher NPL ratios post-injection, consistent with moral hazard
_ground_truth.main_effect: 20bp increase in NPL ratio for TARP banks
